definition: Haughty means arrogantly superior and disdainful.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word haughty. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know haughty should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The soprano's haughty glance at the second violins said, more clearly than words, that she considered them furniture.
Proud can be quiet and deserved - pride in your work looks down on no one, while haughty always finds someone beneath it.
Contemptuous goes further than haughty: the haughty diner looks down on the waiter, while the contemptuous one sneers at him out loud.

Arrogant means claiming superiority - talking over people, assuming you deserve the first and last word - and it can be loud or entirely matter-of-fact. Haughty is one visible flavor of arrogance: cold, silent, and worn on the face, all lifted chin and withering glance.

Snobbish looks down through one narrow lens: class and taste - the right schools, the right shoes, the right accent. Haughty needs no checklist; it is a general air of icy superiority that can descend on anyone at all, whatever their standing or style.

Lofty means elevated and grand - lofty peaks, lofty ideals - and only sometimes sneers; a lofty goal can be admirable. Haughty is never a compliment: the elevation is all in the chin, and its one purpose is to place other people below it.

Haughty comes from French haut, 'high' - still visible in haute cuisine, 'high cooking.' Because the root ends in t, adding the adjective suffix -y produces -ty and lays a perfect trap: haughty looks like an -ity noun and is neither. No everyday English word shares the root.
Haughty means arrogantly superior and disdainful.

At the farmers market, the new cheese vendor waved away questions with a haughty little sigh, explaining that customers who had to ask the price 'were not really her customers.' Stall neighbors who offered friendly advice got the same look, delivered over the same raised chin.
Haughty is sharper than proud: pride can be quiet, private, even earned.
Haughty is pride turned outward and downward - it needs someone to look down on.
The chin lifts precisely so the eyes can descend.
Haughty is vivid and a touch literary - the word for visible, chilly superiority: the lifted chin, the withering glance.
Arrogant is the everyday workhorse; snobbish targets class and taste.
Reach for haughty when you want readers to see the look on the face.

Interns at the Maison Verel were warned about the creative director before they met her.
Madame Verel rarely raised her voice and never argued.
Disapproval arrived as a lifted chin, a slow blink, and a silence that could refit an entire collection overnight.
Fashion writers called her haughty, and the word fit: the icy look fell on duchesses and delivery drivers alike.
One apprentice kept a tally and found the director had spoken forty-one words in a week, thirty of them to her dog.
Yet those who lasted noticed something: the chin never lifted at honest mistakes, only at shortcuts.
Her scorn had standards, even if her warmth did not exist.
